title: Connect Four is solved
hook: Go first, start in the middle column, play perfectly, and you always win.
peek: In 1988 two researchers, working separately, proved that Connect Four is a win for the first player. The winning line starts in the middle column. Start anywhere else and a perfect opponent can at least hold you to a draw.
lede: Connect Four, sold by Milton Bradley from 1974, has a grid of seven columns and six rows. It looks too simple to hide a secret, yet it has more than 4 trillion possible positions. In October 1988, James Dow Allen and Victor Allis independently showed that the first player can always force a win, as long as the first disc goes in the middle column.

bullets.text: Allen announced his result on 1 October 1988, and Allis followed about two weeks later. Allis, then a student in the Netherlands, built a program called Victor that combined computer search with strategic rules that strong players use.
Where the first disc goes matters. Opening in a column next to the centre lets a perfect opponent force a draw, and opening in any of the four outer columns hands the win to the second player.
Even the first player cannot win quickly. Against the best defence, the winning line takes most of the game, and the final four-in-a-row arrives only when the board is nearly full.
Today a small program can play Connect Four perfectly on an ordinary laptop. Online solvers show, for any position, whether it is a win, loss or draw with best play.
